characters.description: Every recurring PERSON/creature in the story. Purely visual, canonical, story-wide identity — this is what every later prompt re-states.

description.description: Fixed visual identity ONLY: apparent age, sex, build/height, skin tone, face shape, distinctive features, hair (colour/length/style), signature wardrobe and its colours, anything a viewer must see to recognise them. No emotion, no plot, no action.

locations.description: Recurring places/settings. REQUIRED and never empty: each one gets its own generated SETTING PLATE, which LTX MSR takes as the shot's BACKGROUND reference (last slot) — that plate is what stops the same place being rebuilt differently in every shot. Every place any shot is set in must appear here.

description.description: Fixed visual character of the place: architecture/landscape, materials, palette, era, time-of-day feel, defining props.

objects.description: Key recurring props/objects that must stay consistent (a specific lamp, a red coat, a sword).

description.description: Fixed visual identity of the object: form, material, colour, size, distinctive marks, mounting/handle, and how it is lit. A story-critical object (one the plot's physical action hinges on) needs the same rigor as a character description.
